2.
Human capital
development
Opportunity
& Risk
Excellence in
human capital
development can
result in strong
employer branding
and a better culture
of innovation.
Failure to prioritize
human capital
development,
including
attracting and
retaining a diverse
talent pool and
supporting
upskilling,
can constrain
innovation and
limit the company’s
ability to respond
to evolving market
demands.
	 Talent discovery- We follow a non-
traditional approach to talent discovery
that depends mainly on employee
referrals which, in our experience,
improves the quality of hires. We also
leverage traditional channels such as
networking sites, job portals, campus
placements and partnerships with
external organizations to tap into diverse
pools of talent.
	 Championing a culture of learning
by doing- To support fast-paced
innovation, Eternal’s culture emphasizes
ownership and autonomy over technical
qualifications. The organization actively
supports the movement of people into
roles where they may not have prior
exposure but have the willingness and
commitment to learn. Employees are
encouraged to demonstrate a founders’
mindset and take ownership of problems
well outside their department or comfort
zone. We reward employees for both
positive outcomes and failures. We
also invest in learning and development
programs - both offline and online - to
enable employees to upskill for evolving
business requirements.
Positive and negative
implication-
Strong performance
in human capital
development results
in better talent and
lower hiring costs.
Gaps in human capital
development can lead
to higher recruitment
and training costs,
while limited workforce
diversity may hinder
ability to respond
to evolving market
demands.

Health, safety,
and dignity
for all
Risk
Ensuring a safe and
respectful working
environment
is core to how
we operate.
Inadequate health
& safety measures
can lead to injuries
or casualties
affecting well-
being. This may
also lead to higher
attrition and loss
of stakeholder
trust. Failure to
uphold human
rights, including
health & safety,
can further expose
the company to
regulatory risks,
with implications
for business
continuity.
	 Employees and workers- Our
occupational health & safety framework
is supported through a comprehensive
policy and robust workplace safety
systems. These include mandatory
training for employees and workers
on health & safety, fire detection
& fire fighting mechanisms, safety
signage and the Safety Reporting
System (SRS) for proactive incident
reporting and resolution. We have
secured ISO 45001:2018 certification
for the Occupational Health and Safety
Management systems in our Gurugram
and Bengaluru leased offices. Please
refer to Principle 3, Essential indicator 10
for more details.
	 Delivery partners
	 Road safety awareness and training-
All delivery partners are required to
complete a mandatory road safety
awareness module at the time of
onboarding. This is supplemented by
periodic health & safety programs
conducted through both online and
offline formats. Delivery partners
also receive educational content and
videos on safe riding practices under
varied weather conditions such as rain,
heat and fog. In addition, we regularly
organize safety camps in collaboration
with local traffic authorities and
have partnered with the Ministry of
Road Transport and Highways for the
national campaign ‘Sadak Suraksha
Abhiyan’ promoting responsible road
behavior among delivery partners and
encouraging customers not to rush
them.
	 SOS service- An SOS service,
accessible via the delivery partner
app, is available to provide immediate
support to all delivery partners in
case of emergencies, including
accidents, vehicle breakdowns, etc.
The SOS service is set up to provide
free ambulance to partners in 900+
cities, depending on the emergency.
Ambulances are positioned to reach
partners within 20 minutes.
	 Insurance coverage- Eternal
voluntarily provides accidental and
medical insurance coverage, inclusive
of disability and death benefits for all
active delivery partners. The premium
for this insurance is borne entirely by
Eternal.
Negative implication-
Inadequate health
& safety measures
across operations can
increase the risk of
work-related injuries or
casualties, adversely
affecting well-being.
Failure to uphold
human rights, including
the right to safe
working conditions,
may lead to business
disruptions, regulatory
penalties, legal
liabilities and cause
reputational damage,
resulting in negative
financial impact.

Innovation
Opportunity
	 Chef’s table experience- A thoughtfully
curated multi-course dining-at-
home experience from some of the
finest restaurants, delivered directly
to customers’ homes. Each menu
is designed to bring the restaurant
experience home, with premium course-
wise packaging for a ‘Meal for 2’. The
program is live in Delhi NCR, Mumbai and
Bengaluru across 250+ restaurant brands
and 650+ outlets.
	 Zomato for Enterprise (ZFE)- ZFE is
a platform designed for companies to
solve food expense management. A lot
of Zomato orders placed by corporate
employees are business-related and need
to be reimbursed by their employer via
processes that are often, cumbersome
and time-consuming. With ZFE,
employees can simply bill their business
orders directly to their employer, without
having to pay, adding convenience
for employees and transparency for
companies. Over 350 companies have
adopted ZFE.
	 Food on Train- Long-distance Indian rail
carries enormous passenger volumes,
yet onboard catering has limited choices
and inconsistent quality. Zomato’s Food
on Train service fixes this through its
IRCTC partnership: customers order
on the app, enter their PNR, and pick a
station along the route, and Zomato’s
station walkers hand the order over right
at the coach gate. Delivering this service
meant building real-time train tracking
and a dedicated layer of walker logistics
synced to each station halt. Zomato
delivers at 250+ stations, pan-India.

7. 	 Statement by director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding

At Eternal, we approach sustainability with the same ambition, patience and discipline we apply to building the business. We are cognizant of our responsibility in setting a
high bar in this domain for new-age, home-grown, technology companies, like ourselves. This BRSR report showcases our progress in FY26 and reflects our commitment
to grow in ways that are responsible, inclusive and sustainable.
In FY26, we conducted a double materiality assessment with an independent external organization to refresh our material ESG topics. The assessment considered the
impact of our business on people and the environment, and the implications of sustainability-related issues on long-term value creation. Our sustainability framework has,
accordingly, been refreshed and re-organized under 4 key pillars: Climate Action and Circular Economy, Inclusive Growth, Responsible Business Leadership and Corporate
Governance. I’ll be sharing ESG highlights from the food delivery business as per the refreshed framework.
Our work on Climate Action and Circular Economy focuses on minimizing our environmental impacts while preparing the business for changes in climate and resource
availability. A key climate risk mitigation action is enabling EV-based deliveries. In FY26, total EV-based food deliveries stood at 132.3 million orders, 13.5% of total FY26
food delivery orders and a 50% increase from the previous year. This achievement rode on the back of expanded EV ecosystem partnerships and the launch of our own
EV rental fleet to match the mobility needs of delivery workers, often migrants seeking to participate in the platform on a part-time and short-term basis. In addition to
our own efforts, the speed of this transition will require coordinated public and private stakeholder action to ensure the right EV products, adequate charging/swapping
infrastructure and affordable financing are made available to anyone who seeks to participate and earn from deliveries.
We are working to reduce both food and packaging waste generated by the food delivery business. Since launch in FY25, Zomato’s Food Rescue feature has helped prevent
over 7.5 lakh kg of food waste by diverting cancelled orders to interested buyers. To reduce the environmental impact of restaurant packaging, we launched Zomato’s
Plastic-Free Future Program in 2024 and have recognized more than 10,000 restaurants with a ‘low plastic packaging’ tag for switching out of plastic to pack their main
menu items . Cumulative orders from restaurants using sustainable packaging crossed 100 million in FY26.

parts.text:
You extract checkable facts from documents so they can later be compared across
documents. You work on any kind of document. Do not assume a subject area.

A fact is worth extracting when it is specific, checkable against this text, and
would still be meaningful to someone who had not read the surrounding page.
Prefer facts that another document could plausibly also state: measured
quantities, identifiers, dates, roles and statuses, named properties of things.

Rules you must follow.

1. Quote verbatim. `quote` must be copied character for character from the text
   you were given, long enough to contain the value and enough words to locate
   it. Never write a character offset, a page number, or a paraphrase.
2. Never calculate. Do not add, convert, rescale, or restate a number in
   different units. Copy `raw` exactly as written, including separators,
   currency symbols, parentheses and any leading comparison operator.
3. Conditions go in `qualifiers`, never folded into the predicate. Any
   circumstance under which the value holds is a qualifier: the time period or
   as-at date it covers, the entity scope it aggregates, the basis or
   measurement convention, the segment, the geography, the units context. Use
   whatever keys the document implies. Invent a key when you need one, but reuse
   an obvious key rather than coining a synonym.
4. Mark qualifier provenance honestly. `stated` means it is in the passage
   itself. `inherited` means you took it from the enclosing context block.
   Never guess a qualifier that neither source supports. Omitting it is correct.
5. Split compound statements into separate facts, one value each.
6. Abstain when the correct reading is genuinely unclear. If a number's meaning,
   subject or period cannot be determined from the passage plus its context, do
   not emit it. A missing fact is cheap; a wrong one is not. Lower `confidence`
   when you are unsure rather than inflating it.
7. `predicate` is lower snake_case naming the relation alone, with no period,
   entity, scale or unit inside it. `subject_key` is a hard identifier only when
   the document supplies one; otherwise leave it null.
8. `subject_surface` is the thing the value belongs to, never the name of the
   measurement. In a table, the row label names the property and the subject is
   whatever the table is about - the organisation, place, product or person the
   document is reporting on. Name that subject even when it is stated only in a
   heading, a page header or the document's title. Use the fullest form of its
   name that appears, and use the same form every time it recurs.

Return only facts supported by the passage. Returning an empty list is a valid
answer for a passage that states nothing checkable.
